title: Azam Khan Gets Four Days in ED Custody, Faces Lucknow Questioning Friday
excerpt: A Ghaziabad special court gave the ED four days' custody of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan, until November 16, 2026, in the money-laundering investigation linked to Jauhar University. Khan is to be brought to Lucknow for questioning.
body:
• A Ghaziabad special court granted the Enforcement Directorate four days' custody of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan, from 4:30 p.m. on November 12 to 4:30 p.m. on November 16, 2026.
  • Khan is to be brought to Lucknow on Friday for questioning in the money-laundering investigation linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and its trust.
  • Azam Khan said at his arrest that this was the punishment for being a Muslim and that a Muslim building a university was treated as a crime, as reported by the Times of India via DailyGraph.
  • The ED case is an allegation under investigation; the custody order is not a finding of guilt.

The Enforcement Directorate has secured four days of custody of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan in a money-laundering investigation linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. According to the remand order reported by ANI via Indian Economic Observer, ED custody runs for four days, from November 12 at 4:30 p.m. to November 16 at 4:30 p.m., and Khan will be brought to Lucknow on Friday for questioning.

IANS via hi INDiA reported that a special court in Ghaziabad sent Khan to ED custody for four days in the Rs 426 crore money-laundering case linked to the university, and that he is likely to be brought to Lucknow from Dasna jail on Friday by the agency for questioning, according to an official.

What Azam Khan said

Khan's own reaction was reported when the ED arrested him outside Rampur district jail on October 31, shortly after his release there. As ED officials questioned him outside the jail, Khan said, according to a Times of India report republished by DailyGraph:

"What more can I say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. That is our crime."

Aaj Tak's Hindi headline on the latest development carried a related remark attributed to Khan, describing the building of a "temple of education" by a Muslim as his mistake. The remark is Khan's statement about his own case, reported here as a statement; the ED's allegations, set out below, are likewise reported as the agency's case, not as established fact.

The investigation as the ED describes it

The agency says its investigation concerns alleged diversion of government contract funds through private contractors, and the subsequent use of those funds, including for the creation of assets of the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Before his apprehension, the ED had questioned Khan on October 13 at Rampur jail and recorded his statement as part of that investigation.

The probe follows searches conducted by the ED on August 19 at 10 premises linked to Khan in Uttar Pradesh and Delhi, under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, covering locations in Rampur and Saharanpur, including premises associated with the trust and the university. According to the ED, contractors who allegedly benefited from government contracts diverted funds towards the trust and the university through donations and construction work.

On October 28, the ED attached the land and building of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The agency put the book value of the attached property at Rs 426 crore, while its estimated current market value was Rs 1,170 crore. IANS put the provisionally attached amount at Rs 426.46 crore and said the agency claims those assets represent alleged proceeds of crime. The university, founded by Khan in 2006, is a private university in Rampur, owned by the trust, which Khan founded and controls and of which he is honorary Chancellor, according to IANS.

How Khan came to be in custody

The ED apprehended Khan on October 31, shortly after his release from Rampur district jail, when a team from the agency's Lucknow zonal office reached the jail premises. He was then remanded to judicial custody and lodged in Dasna jail. On November 5, the Supreme Court declined to grant him immediate relief in his plea challenging the ED arrest and asked him to approach the Allahabad High Court, with the petition listed before a Division Bench on November 16, IANS reported.

Khan, a 10-time MLA from Rampur Sadar and a former Cabinet minister, is one of the Samajwadi Party's prominent leaders in Uttar Pradesh. The four-day ED custody now runs to November 16, the same date as the High Court listing reported by IANS, with questioning in Lucknow the next step reported by both agencies.
nri_angle: Developments in a major Uttar Pradesh political and university case, reported with the ED's allegations and Khan's own statement kept distinct.
author: Diaspora Desk
